from rich.console import Console


def test_soft_wrap_background_color():
    console = Console()
    
    # Capture the output of the first print with soft_wrap=True
    from io import StringIO
    import sys
    output = StringIO()
    sys.stdout = output
    console.print("soft wrap is on", style="blue on white", soft_wrap=True)
    console.print("still has background color from previous line")
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    
    # Check the output
    printed_output = output.getvalue()
    print(repr(printed_output))  # Debugging line to see the actual output
    assert printed_output == 'soft wrap is on\nstill has background color from previous line\n'  # Check if output is as expected
    
    # Capture the output of the second print with soft_wrap=False
    output = StringIO()
    sys.stdout = output
    console.print("soft wrap is off", style="blue on white", soft_wrap=False)
    console.print("correctly has no color from previous line")
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    
    # Check the output
    printed_output = output.getvalue()
    print(repr(printed_output))  # Debugging line to see the actual output
    assert printed_output == 'soft wrap is off\ncorrectly has no color from previous line\n'  # Check if output is as expected
